title: 3-2-1: On spotting new opportunities, the power of high volume, and how to make a big decision
author: James Clear
summary: This issue of James Clear's weekly 3-2-1 newsletter offers three short ideas of his own, two quotations from other writers, and one question, all circling how to find opportunities and commit to them. Clear first ties mental toughness to genuine interest, arguing that persistence comes more easily when the subject is right. He then gives a three-part method for seeing opportunities others miss: borrow from a different field, invert the problem, and spend time with highly creative people. His third idea is about volume, contrasting the person who needs one shot to go perfectly with the person whose many attempts make eventual success likely. Quotations from Hunter S. Thompson and Ursula K. Le Guin reinforce the themes of daring and of valuing the journey, and the closing question offers a heuristic for big decisions: whether the choice would make you feel more alive.
points: Clear links mental toughness to interest, suggesting persistence is partly a matter of choosing the right subject.
His method for spotting overlooked opportunities combines cross-domain borrowing, inverting the problem, and proximity to hyper-creative people.
Structuring your work to get many attempts beats needing a single attempt to go perfectly.
The closing heuristic for major decisions asks whether a choice would make you feel more alive.
quotes: Mental toughness immediately increases when you find the right subject. You’re more likely to stick with things when you’re genuinely interested.
Study a totally different field, then return to the original problem. Apply insights from other domains.
The person who gets 1 shot needs everything to go right. The person who gets 1000 shots is going to score at some point.
Find a way to play the game that ensures you get a lot of shots.
Who is the happier man, he who has braved the storm of life and lived, or he who has stayed securely on shore and merely existed?
It is good to have an end to journey towards; but it is the journey that matters, in the end.
A good heuristic when making a big decision: would choosing this make me feel more alive?
